name: OPA1611 / OPA1612 (TI SoundPlus bipolar-input, 1.1 nV/√Hz single/dual)
tagline: TI's 1.1 nV/√Hz bipolar audio op-amp with −136 dB THD+N at 1 kHz. It is widely used for I/V conversion and buffering in modern DACs, DAPs and Hi-Fi phones.
technology: Bipolar-input, voltage-feedback op-amp, unity-gain stable. The output is rail-to-rail (within 0.6 V at 2 kΩ, 0.2 V at 10 kΩ). The inputs have back-to-back differential clamp diodes. Copper leadframe (SBOS450C §7.3.1). Rev A (Aug 2009) and Rev B (Jul 2011) front pages carry 'Burr-Brown Audio' branding and the title 'High-Performance Bipolar-Input AUDIO OPERATIONAL AMPLIFIERS'; web search shows this in the mirror titles. Rev C (Aug 2014) is titled 'OPA161x SoundPlus™'. TI's current parametric listing still tags the part 'Burr-Brown™ Audio'. The OPA1611 comes in SOIC-8 (D) only. The OPA1612 comes in SOIC-8 (D) or SON-8 3×3 mm (DRG), which TI's parametric table calls WSON. No DIP package appears in the datasheet or the orderable addendum.
manufacturers: Texas Instruments (Burr-Brown Audio / SoundPlus product line)

reputation.summary: Its measured noise and distortion are exceptional (1.1 nV/√Hz, −136 dB THD+N), and measurement-oriented users treat it as essentially transparent (discovery note). In audioXpress 'Modern Op-Amp Distortion Tests, Part 1' (author not confirmed here), the OPA1612 showed less distortion than the NE5532 with shunt feedback and much less as a voltage follower, but about the same with series feedback. Soomal teardowns show it spreading through Chinese Hi-Fi phones and DAPs from 2014: FiiO X5, Meizu MX4 Pro, vivo X5 Max, Xiaomi Note and Smartisan T2. In 2022 Soomal said a very large share of recent products use the OPA1612 for I/V conversion. Japanese hobbyists call it a neutral 'reference sound' all-rounder (discovery note, not verified). The subjective camp is split. Soomal found it 'hard, not pleasing' (偏硬，不够讨喜) in a 2020 AE-9 op-amp swap, though with better dynamics and resolution than the NE5534. In 2016 Soomal argued that bipolar parts like the OPA1612 sound worse on average than DiFET types, and that passage mislabels the OPA1612 as 'Bipolar FET'.
sonic_descriptors: neutral / 'reference sound' (JP, maimai-audio; discovery note, unverified)
flat, not genre-dependent (JP owners; discovery note, unverified)
musical, delicate and warm (OPA1611; Audiogon thread per discovery note; low confidence)
hard / 偏硬, not pleasing (Soomal 2020, AE-9 op-amp swap, where it is written 'OP1611')
better dynamics and resolution than NE5534 (same Soomal 2020 passage)
average sound worse than DiFET types (Soomal 2016, 901 player / MINIBOX review)
typical_uses: DAC I/V conversion: Sabaj A20d (2022), with three OPA1612 for I/V and separate op-amps marked '2149U' doing the LPF, and Topping DX7 Pro (both per Soomal 2022)
Output LPF in DAPs (SoundAware MR1 with dual CS4398, per Soomal 2017)

Post-I/V amplifier or buffer in Hi-Fi phones and DAPs: Meizu MX4 Pro (2014), vivo X5 Max (2014), Xiaomi Note (2015, after ADA4896 I/V), Smartisan T2 (2016, two OPA1612 replacing one OPA2604), FiiO X5 (2014, with an LMH6643 buffer), all per Soomal
Input or error amplifier in VFA-CFA composite headphone amps with TPA6120 or THS6012 (e.g. the PWieland/SCAM project)
Professional audio, microphone preamps, mixing consoles, broadcast gear, audio test equipment and A/V receivers (TI's listed applications)
Op-amp rolling via DIP-8 adapter boards
caveats: Current noise is fairly high (1.7 pA/√Hz @1 kHz). With source or feedback networks of 10 kΩ or more it loses its noise advantage over FET-input parts, as a JP hobbyist's 2026 design notes (indare/pcb_work) also found.
The input common-mode range stops 2 V from each rail, so G = +1 buffers clip early on low supplies.
The back-to-back input diodes can conduct on fast edges in low-gain or G = +1 circuits. TI says to limit input current to 10 mA.
At low gain, capacitive loads reduce phase margin and can cause peaking or oscillation; TI suggests about 50 Ω series isolation (§8.4). Layout and decoupling on DIP adapters matter.
Iq is 3.6 mA per channel and θJA of SOIC-8 is 150 °C/W. TI says soldering rather than socketing reduces temperature rise.
It comes only in SOIC or SON, so every 'DIP' part is an adapter board. Relabelled TL082 fakes are documented (diyAudio 332536).
The audioXpress advantage over the NE5532 depends on topology: it is clear for shunt feedback and followers, and about equal with series feedback.
The subjective descriptors conflict with each other, and no controlled listening test was verified.

revision_history.changes: Initial release. The date comes from the 'JULY 2009' origin line in later headers. No copy was found, and the original→A changes are not recorded in Rev C.

The header is confirmed by web mirrors (Reichelt, BDTIC and alldatasheet 311775, per search summaries). The front page carries 'Burr-Brown Audio' branding, the title 'High-Performance Bipolar-Input AUDIO OPERATIONAL AMPLIFIERS' and the 'IN- Pre-Output Driver' layout; the alldatasheet copy has 21 pages. The Rev C log does not record what changed from the original.

The header is confirmed by the Octopart 21221010 copy (web search summary). A→B, per the Rev C change log: revised Features list; updated front-page figure; added a max spec for input voltage noise density at 1 kHz (1.5 nV/√Hz); corrected a typo in EC footnote 1; revised Figures 4, 7, 9, 11, 15 and 29; revised the Electrical Overstress section; revised the table in Figure 34. No absolute-max, pinout or silicon change is indicated. 'Burr-Brown Audio' branding is retained.

B→C: new TI datasheet format; added the SON-8 (DRG) package (IB max ±300 nA for DRG); renamed SO to SOIC; added the front-page curve; added a block-diagram title; replaced the Package Information table with the addendum. The title became 'OPA161x SoundPlus™'. Still current in Sep 2026 per web search: gpn/OPA1612 serves SBOS450C and no SBOS450D was found. TI refreshed only the addendum and T&R pages, dated 10-Nov-2025.

OPA1612-Q1 automotive datasheet (AEC-Q100 Grade 1, SOIC-8). Confirmed by web search in Sep 2026 and by TI's PSpice model header (24AUG2022). The original SLOS931 and the original→A changes were not seen.

Corroboration only. A search summary says the Qobuz copy (static.qobuz.com/info/IMG/pdf/opa1611.pdf) contains the 'Changes from Revision A (August 2009) to Revision B' log. That makes the copy Rev B, not just a probable Rev B, and confirms that Rev A is dated August 2009. The changes themselves were not shown beyond what the Rev C log already records.

silicon_changes.when: PCN# 20260223007.1 dated 24 Feb 2026; estimated sample availability 25 Apr 2026; proposed first ship 25 May 2026
silicon_changes.identification: Same part number, same die and datasheet (SBOS450C unchanged). This is an assembly-material change that adds Cu as an alternative bond-wire metal, staying at the current assembly facility with piece-part changes. No external marking cue is documented, so lots shipped after about 25 May 2026 may carry either wire metal. OPA1612AID was seen in the product-affected list, which is mixed (roughly 40 devices: OPA2187, OPA2210, OPA4140, INA18x/INA8xx, DACx0004, TLV417x, TPS65910; SOIC, TSSOP and QFN). OPA1611 orderables and other OPA1612 orderables were not confirmed on the list.
silicon_changes.summary: TI PCN# 20260223007.1, 'Add Cu as Alternative Wire Base Metal for Selected Device(s)', qualifies Cu as an additional bond-wire option 'to align with world technology trends and use wiring with enhanced mechanical properties'. It has 60-day acknowledgment and sample-request windows. It is not a fab, process or die revision, so it is not a silicon change for OPA1612. No other OPA1611/OPA1612 PCN (fab, die or datasheet) was found.

spec_deltas.before: existing wire metal (Au presumed, not verified)
spec_deltas.after: Cu added as an alternative bond wire

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Negligible. A bond-wire metal option does not change the op-amp's electrical design, and no datasheet revision followed as of Sep 2026. Claims of an audible difference would be anecdotal.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low - assembly-material option only; same die, pinout and datasheet
silicon_changes.verification: Merged three reports of the same PCN. WebSearch confirmed the title and 24 Feb 2026 date via Mouser and Farnell copies; OPA1611 inclusion was not independently confirmed, and a search for OPA161x fab or die-revision PCNs only turned up generic RFAB/FFAB PCNs with no OPA161x listing seen.

counterfeit_notes: Confirmed by web search in diyAudio thread 332536 ('Fake OPA1612 from China'): a buyer bought 10 'OPA1612' from a Chinese eBay seller for €6.80 in total. Under the microscope they turned out to be relabelled TL082 JFET dies, identified by the cross-shaped 'butterfly' FET input devices, not bipolar OPA1612 dies. A TI E2E thread, 'OPA1612 - Fake chips?' (532783), exists; its content was not seen. diyAudio thread 399994 ('OPA1612 from Aliexpress, no counterfeit but why so cheap?') reports cheap AliExpress parts that decapped as genuine OPA1612 dies, so cheap does not always mean fake. The roughly 150 nA input bias reported there (discovery note) is inside the ±250 nA max. Screening tips from the datasheet: (1) TI lists only SOIC-8 (D) and, for the OPA1612, SON-8 (DRG), so a DIP-8 body marked OPA161x is not a TI package. (2) The genuine SOIC top mark is 'OPA' over '1611A' or '1612A', and the DRG mark is 'OVII'. (3) Iq should be about 3.6 mA per channel, 4.5 mA max. (4) Input bias should be tens of nA; pA-level bias points to a JFET relabel. (5) Noise should be about 1.1 nV/√Hz, so a relabelled TL08x is roughly ten times noisier. Buy from TI or authorised distributors.

No other fab, assembly or die-change PCN for OPA1611/OPA1612 was found. TI's 2022–2023 RFAB/FFAB PCNs surfaced in search, but none was shown to include OPA161x.
The original SBOS450 (no letter, Jul 2009) has not been found, and the original→A changes are unknown.

The Rev A/B assignment of the pre-2014 mirrors rests on search summaries and front-page layout: 'IN- Pre-Output Driver' layout is Rev A (Reichelt, BDTIC, ic114); 'Pre-Output Driver OUT V- V+' layout is Rev B (Octopart 21221010, Qobuz). The Mouser opa1612-200626 copy still needs its header checked.
TI's revision-specific URLs (sbos450a/b/c, slos931/slos931a) and the focus.ti.com symlinks are inferred archive seeds and were not seen.
audioXpress says the OPA1612 was 'introduced in 2011', while the datasheet dates from July 2009; this may refer to market launch. The article's author was not confirmed as Douglas Self.
The Rev C datasheet contradicts itself on output drive: ±30 mA on the front page against ±40 mA in §7.1. TI's parametric table gives 55 mA 'Iout typ', which matches ISC +55 mA.
DRG (SON-8) has an IB max of ±300 nA against ±250 nA for SOIC. It is presumably the same die with package-related guard-banding, which TI does not state.
The OPA1612AQDRQ1 lifecycle flag was not seen; only a live TI part-details page was.
The maimai-audio 'reference sound' description, the Audiogon descriptors and the content of the TI E2E fake-chip thread (532783) were not re-read.

revision_chain_notes:
I used all 5 WebSearch calls. The main gaps did not close: no copy of the unlettered July 2009 SBOS450 original turned up, and there is no sign of an SBOS450D.

TI SBOS450 (OPA1611 and OPA1612 share one datasheet; there is no separate OPA1612 document), oldest to newest:
1. **Original, July 2009.** Still missing. The only lead is the protricom.hu copy. Its front page reads 'Burr-Brown Audio IN- Pre-Output Driver OUT IN+ V- V+', the same as the Rev A copies, so it could be the original or Rev A. Its header has not been seen.
2. **SBOS450A, revised August 2009.** Found in the Reichelt, BDTIC and ic114 copies (ic114 is now named as Rev A in a search summary) and alldatasheet 311775 (PDF page and HTML page view).
3. **SBOS450B, revised July 2011.** Found in Octopart 21221010 and the Qobuz copy. The Qobuz copy is now confirmed by its 'Changes from Revision A (August 2009) to Revision B' log.
4. **SBOS450C, revised August 2014.** This is the current revision. It is served at ti.com/lit/pdf/sbos450 (confirmed by a search summary), the ti.com and ti.com.cn symlinks, and datasheet4u 1413230.

A search that included "SBOS450D" found nothing, so C still appears to be current. The original→A changes are still undocumented.

TI SLOS931 (OPA1612-Q1):
- The original SLOS931 is missing.
- **SLOS931A (November 2015, revised November 2015)** is current. New mirrors were found at mouser.lt, datasheetspdf and datasheet4u 1413232, but none of their snippets shows a revision.

Two unconfirmed points:
- Two search summaries said the output drive is ±30 mA and one said ±40 mA. None tied either value to a specific revision, so nothing was recorded.
- The archive_seed_urls follow TI's legacy URL patterns (the focus.ti.com and www.ti.com symlinks, and the lit/ds/sbos450{,a,b} revision-specific paths). They are meant for Wayback lookups and were not seen in search results. The one exception is ti.com/lit/pdf/sbos450, which was seen.

Suggested next step: check Wayback captures from 2009 to 2011 of focus.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa1611.pdf and opa1612.pdf, and of www.ti.com/lit/ds/sbos450/sbos450.pdf, for the unlettered original. Also check the header of the protricom.hu copy.
